profile_text.body:
AssistiveWare describes itself as a builder of AAC apps that shares best practices to help people communicate with the world, working closely with the Augmentative and Alternative Communication community. Its site discusses core words in AAC systems, Gestalt Language Processing, and stories such as that of Jordyn Zimmerman, and it hosts an interactive feature called The Land of Autistic Communication, including an animated location called the Mountains of Echolalia. A support team member, Lily Konyn, is credited with writing about Gestalt Language Processing.

The company's tracked product is Proloquo2Go, listed under Education and Research AI, which the vendor describes as using word prediction. It is aimed at students with communication needs and speech-language pathologists, with an App Store age rating of 4+ and a vendor description for users aged 2 and up. The vendor states usage data is collected anonymously, while the App Store label lists identifiers and usage data not linked to identity, and no school account is needed. Pricing is $249.99 on the App Store, with optional Gateway vocabulary at $149.99 as of May 2026.

The held record lists no lawsuits and no MCP servers for AssistiveWare.
